rows.source: Independent five-row-method Hess refit from ilmenite crystal formation Gibbs, measured fusion thermochemistry, and Kirchhoff liquid heat capacity; A refit with B fixed.
rows.T_domain_basis: sf04-exercised-ADOPTED (v1.0.2: FC87 fits were exercised by SF04 over 1700-3000 K; the FC87-paper-demonstrated span is preserved in T_domain_paper_demonstrated_K)
rows.derivation: Mixing-inclusive Hess refit to pure-ilmenite liquid Gibbs targets at 1600, 1800, and 2000 K, constructed from Robie & Hemingway (1995) crystal G nodes, Naylor & Cook (1946) fusion/heat-content data, the Robie, Hemingway & Fisher (1978) liquid Cp, and the current parent-liquid standards. The five-row-method model includes ideal associate mixing entropy and every associate extent-weighted reaction Gibbs term. B is held at 5019.995948414166 K; bounded least squares gives ΔA = −1.0830119847925224. The post-fit model-minus-target leftovers are −3.523, +0.496, and +3.831 kJ mol-1 at 1600, 1800, and 2000 K. The target model liquid Gibbs energies are −34.791257, −36.055027, and −37.974733 kJ mol-1 at 1600, 1800, and 2000 K; the constant ilmenite liquid Cp is 199.16 J mol-1 K-1.

rows.source: Independent fayalite Hess comparison using the Robie & Hemingway crystal heat-capacity polynomial printed on USGS Bulletin 2131, p. 60, the Stebbins & Carmichael fusion enthalpy, Kirchhoff liquid heat capacity, and the current parent-liquid standards; the A-only fit reaches its lower bound.
rows.T_domain_basis: sf04-exercised-ADOPTED (v1.0.2: FC87 fits were exercised by SF04 over 1700-3000 K; the FC87-paper-demonstrated span is preserved in T_domain_paper_demonstrated_K)
rows.derivation: The rebuilt crystal-plus-fusion liquid targets are -27.026, -25.524, and -24.553 kJ mol-1 at 1600, 1800, and 2000 K. The printed crystal Cp values are 204.0 and 210.1 J mol-1 K-1 at 1300 and 1400 K; the earlier calculation inherited 191 J mol-1 K-1. The fitted A is at the lower Delta-A bound of -8, giving A=-9.744444812 with B fixed at 5946.762412921802 K. This is the no-association limit, K tending to zero: at fayalite composition the liquid is ideal FeO-SiO2 mixing, and the Hess nodes identify neither a finite association constant nor its temperature slope. The ideal mixing ceilings are -25.403, -28.578, and -31.754 kJ mol-1 formula at those temperatures. The 1800 and 2000 K targets exceed the ceiling by 3.05 and 7.20 kJ mol-1, so no association constant can reach them; they imply about 5-11 kJ mol-1 of positive excess Gibbs energy, which is not included. Under v5, the associate is 37-40 kJ mol-1 formula too stable against the crystal-plus-fusion targets. At 1300/1400 K, the fayalite crystal saturation indices are +0.84/+0.46 versus about -1.3 under v5; these temperatures are below the 1700 K association floor. A full-composition, Fe-saturated comparison against all 24 Distin–Whiteway reported activities gives median absolute log activity residuals of 0.179 dex under v5 and 0.019 dex here, with mean signed residuals of -0.153 and -0.009.

Aligned 34 FC87 rows with the SF04-exercised runtime interval [1700, 3000] K. The paper-demonstrated interval remains in T_domain_paper_demonstrated_K; coefficients are unchanged.

Translated four FC87 K rows to the packaged JANAF K-012 and K2O(l) fusion reference while holding absolute complex Gibbs energy fixed. Three rows with unknown references remain active and flagged; 30 rows retain published coefficients. KCaAlSi2O7 retains its established treatment.

For FeO(l), the selected Darken and Gurry (1946) iron-saturated equilibria reduced via Masson (1965) give dG = 27778.965828 - 10.961554232*T J/mol; this shift is applied to FeO(l), the FeO1.5 oxidation reaction, and Fe-bearing associations. MgAl2O4 row 3 uses Shornikov (2017) Delta_fus_H = 55.81 +/- 4.62 kJ/mol with JANAF Al-089 crystal and Al-090 fusion/Cp. FeAl2O4 row 21 retains its FC87 R21 estimates; redox homologue statistics and the condensate FeO(l) row are updated consistently.
Corrected the FeTiO3, Fe2SiO4, and FeAl2O4 source statements to identify the Darken and Gurry/Masson FeO(l) re-anchor as part of the default pack.
Added source_refs to every default melt row and DOI fields to the referenced source inventory. source_refs is provenance metadata; it does not alter the numerical coefficients.
Promotes measured SiO2(l) and Na2O(l) heat capacities; the prior default 1.0.5-d066-v3 remains available by file id.

Refit constant A values for Mg2SiO4, CaSiO3, CaAl2Si2O8, Ca2MgSi2O7 and MgAl2O4 from independent Hess-cycle liquid formation energies with B fixed; all other association coefficients remain unchanged.

feo_liquid_candidate.source: Source decision: criterion 2 (primary measurements) selects the Darken & Gurry (1946) iron-saturated equilibria, reduced via Masson (1965), over JANAF Fe-019’s 1965 construction. Fe-019 assigns wustite fusion to O2 release at 1 bar. Residuals are reported and never gate this source choice. Darken & Gurry (1946), Tables IIIA/B/VI; Masson (1965), Eq. 17
feo_liquid_candidate.transformation: For each association consuming nu_FeO FeO(l), preserve the complex standard Gibbs energy: log10(K_new/K_old)=nu_FeO*DeltaG_FeO/(R*T*ln(10)); equivalently add nu_FeO*c1/(R ln 10) to A and nu_FeO*c0/(R ln 10) to B.
feo_liquid_candidate.uncertainty: Darken & Gurry report no formal pointwise activity uncertainty; the adopted source correction is fixed and its anchor residuals are reported without using them as a selection gate.
